title: SLO-aware quant policy templates and staged canary for quantized model onboarding
creator: Ethan Brooks
description:
Goal: Build a repeatable, SLO-aware onboarding flow for quantized model artifacts (INT8 / FP8 / GPTQ / AWQ) that publishes performance profiles and gates rollouts via staged canaries tied to latency, p95 token cost, and semantic-quality regressions.

Scope:
- Define canonical policy templates (manifest fields, required benchmarks, acceptable deltas) for each quant family.
- Implement a canary runner that applies staged traffic percentages (1%, 5%, 25%) with automated metric checks and rollback hooks.
- Publish a machine-readable 'quant-artifact manifest' including: base model hash, quant method, calibration data id, expected perf profile (latency/p95, throughput/kgpu), and quality regression tolerances.
- Integrate with existing perf-regression pipeline to run synthetic evals (prompt sets + sampling policy) as part of pre-rollout validation.
- Add telemetry hooks for drift detection and periodic re-evaluation of published profiles.

Acceptance criteria:
- Policy templates for INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ are reviewed and checked into /docs/quant/policies.
- Canary runner deploys a quant variant and enforces automated gates (latency increase <= 10% p95, semantic delta <= 1.5% on eval set) before promoting to broader traffic.
- Published perf profile artifacts are versioned and surfaced in the Console under 'Model -> Profiles' with provenance links.
- Automated alerts trigger and roll back on canary failures; post-deploy regressions create a regression ticket with captured traces and diffs.

Implementation notes / trade-offs:
- We will store manifests as small JSONL artifacts in the artifact store (cheap to query). This avoids changing existing model registry schema.
- Canary checks will initially use synthetic prompt sets (fast, reproducible) and request-level telemetry; we defer user-facing A/B evals to later cycles to reduce privacy complexity.
- Quality gating uses an ensemble of metrics (semantic similarity, token-level perplexity, and regression on a small human-labeled set) to avoid false positives from any single noisy metric.
- For low-latency models, stricter latency gates will be applied; for heavy-batched throughput-first bundles we will relax p95 thresholds but enforce throughput targets.

Rollout plan:
1) Draft policy templates and manifest schema (this ticket).
2) Implement canary runner + metric gates in runtime (feature branch).
3) Run internal dogfood with 3 quantized artifacts across families.
4) Publish profiles to Console + opt teams into automated canaries.

Success metrics:
- Reduction in post-deploy perf regressions attributable to quantized rollouts by 80% vs baseline.
- Time-to-onboard quantized artifact from PR to published profile under 48 hours for <= 2 failures.
- >90% canaries succeed without manual intervention for vetted model families.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Triage: E. Brooks created ticket after last week's incident where AWQ rollout caused p95 spikes for chat-internal; initial scope agreed with PM.

2026-03-03 - Architecture sync: Decided to publish manifest as JSONL in artifact store instead of changing registry. Trade-off: easier iteration vs duplication of some registry metadata. Action: Maya to draft schema.
2026-03-05 - Design review: PM (A. Nguyen) requested clearer customer impact tiers per template (low-latency, high-throughput, safety-sensitive). Added to labels and acceptance criteria.

2026-03-06 - PoC run: Ran staged canary for GPTQ variant of llama-med with 1%, 5% traffic progression. Canary failed at 5% due to 12% p95 regression; auto-rollback executed as expected. Logs: https://dash.redwood.ai/boards/quant-canary/1234
2026-03-08 - PR opened: Implemented canary runner and manifest ingestion. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/4982 (WIP). Needs review from runtime and telemetry owners.

2026-03-09 - Perf test: Synthetic eval harness results attached — semantic delta measured via embeddings similarity lower bound of 0.98 for INT8 on conv-eval set. One false positive flagged; will tune ensemble weighting.
2026-03-10 - Security note: Security requested an audit of manifest fields to ensure no customer PII is embedded in calibration blobs; confirmed calibration stored by id reference only.
notes: Follow-ups: add periodic re-eval job to detect drift and notify model owners.
Consider adding an opt-out flag per workspace for automatic canaries until we reach >2 months reliability stats.
